description.narrative:
In Zanzibar, KTO expanded its partnerships with three ALAE centres and successfully implemented football production training under the Vijana Nguvu Kazi programme in Kizimkazi. The training engaged both young men and women and, following five days of evening sessions, resulted in the establishment of a womens football team. This contributed to increased participation of young women in sports and promoted gender inclusion and empowerment through skills development activities.
At the national level, a key achievement was KTOs leadership in facilitating the accreditation of the Early Childhood Development (ECD) course by NACTVET. KTO also coordinated the implementation of ECD examinations, including post-moderation processes, across 15 Folk Development Colleges. These efforts contributed to improved consistency, fairness, and quality assurance in assessment processes, while generating recommendations for further strengthening future examinations.
KTO further contributed to strengthening the Elimu Haina Mwisho (EHM) programme by supporting the orientation and capacity development required for the integration of the new vocational secondary education curriculum. In collaboration with the Tanzania Institute of Education (TIE), KTO facilitated technical discussions and supported the establishment of a joint working group comprising representatives from FDCs, TVET institutions, and the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST).
Internationally, KTO continued its collaboration with Grimslövs and Sörängens Folk High Schools in Sweden. In 2025, a delegation of 16 Tanzanian FDC representatives, led by the KTO Director and including staff from Ilula and Katumba FDCs, participated in a study visit to the Swedish partner institutions. The exchange provided opportunities for peer learning, exposure to international approaches to adult and vocational education, strengthened institutional networks, and contributed to the continued development of partnerships under the Atlas Planning framework.
